newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower on corn, soy drop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower on corn, soy drop.

text.p: A sharp drop in corn and soybean futures pressured CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
But the market was underpinned by short covering, a firmer technical picture and ongoing talk about concerns about seeding delays due to wet weather, they said.
"There still is wet weather in the Plains so plantings will be delayed," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
The market also featured position squaring before the release Monday of USDA's quarterly stocks report, traders said.
An average of analysts' estimates pegged the U.S. total wheat stocks as of September 1 in the U.S. at 1.767 billion bushels, below the 1.881 billion a year ago.
Technical traders said wheat was oversold late last week and gains this week indicated the market was consolidating and attempting to form a bottom.
Wheat closed 4-1/2 cents a bushel lower to 1/4 higher, with December down 1/4 at $4.29-1/4. March was up 1/4 at $4.21.
Wheat volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, down slightly from 10,203 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Continental Grain bought 400 March $4.20 calls at 24 to 24-3/4 cents and sold 400 March $4.60 calls at 10-1/2 to 11 cents, according to the CBOT.
Options volume was estimated at 3,500 contracts, down from 5,828 Wednesday.
